Options and environment variables used by condathis

Source: R/condathis-options.R
condathis-options.Rd

condathis reads a small set of R options and environment variables to locate micromamba, choose a backend, and resolve its data directories. It also builds an isolated environment for every child process it spawns. That isolation clears or overrides many CONDA_* and MAMBA_* variables, so values set in the calling session never reach micromamba or the tools it runs.

This page leaves out fallbacks that apply only when the variables listed here are unset, such as HOMEDRIVE and HOMEPATH on Windows.

R options

Set these with base::options(), for example in an .Rprofile file.

condathis.micromamba_path

Character string. Path to a micromamba binary to use instead of the one managed by condathis. It has the highest priority in the micromamba discovery order (see micromamba discovery). The binary must report a compatible version. Otherwise, condathis uses the next candidate. Default: NULL (unset).

condathis.backend_priority

Character vector. The order of the registered backends for method = "auto". A new environment goes to the first available backend in this order: in create_env(), and when run(), run_bin(), run_pipeline() or install_packages() create "condathis-env". list_envs() and get_install_dir() report the backends in this order. The vector sets an order, not an allowlist: registered backends missing from the vector come after the listed ones, in alphabetical order. condathis loads a backend package that it knows, such as "rattler" of rattlerthis, when the vector lists the backend and a new environment needs a backend. The vector therefore applies even when nothing else loaded the package. Other names that are not registered are ignored. A value that is not a character vector without NA warns once per session with class condathis_invalid_backend_priority_option and is ignored. Default: "micromamba", so loading another backend package does not change where condathis creates new environments. An existing environment always uses the backend that owns it.

timeout

Numeric. Base R download timeout in seconds. While install_micromamba() downloads the binary, condathis uses the larger of this value and the timeout argument as the limit for each download. The limit applies to both curl and utils::download.file(). Inf, or 0 when both values are 0, means no limit. condathis lowers a finite limit above 2147483 seconds (about 24.8 days) to that value, because older libcurl versions reject larger values. condathis ignores a session value that is not a single, non-negative number. It restores the session value afterwards.

Environment variables read by condathis

Set these in the shell, in an .Renviron file, or with base::Sys.setenv().

CONDATHIS_MICROMAMBA_PATH

Path to a micromamba binary. Same effect as the condathis.micromamba_path option, with lower priority than that option.

CONDA_PREFIX

Prefix of the Conda environment active in the calling shell. condathis reads it only to look for micromamba inside that prefix during discovery. It never passes it on to child processes.

PATH

Searched for micromamba as the last discovery fallback. Also the base PATH for child processes. run_bin() and run_pipeline() prepend the environment's binary directories to it.

PATHEXT

Windows only. Extensions tried when a command name is resolved inside an environment. Default when unset: .COM;.EXE;.BAT;.CMD.

TAR

A system tar program, as used by base R: a program name, looked up on PATH, or the path of an executable file. install_micromamba() extracts the micromamba archive with R's internal tar, and uses this program only when that fails. It skips the value internal, an empty value, and a program that cannot be found or run, and uses tar on PATH instead. TAR does not support arguments.

Environment variables that set data and cache directories

condathis keeps micromamba, its environments and its package cache in the condathis data directory, tools::R_user_dir("condathis", "data") (see get_install_dir()). Every other backend keeps its environments and caches in a directory of its name inside it, such as R/condathis/rattler (see backend_root_dir()). These variables move those directories through the rules of tools::R_user_dir(). Backends have no options or environment variables of their own for them.

R_USER_DATA_DIR

Base data directory. Takes precedence over XDG_DATA_HOME. The condathis data directory is its R/condathis subdirectory.

XDG_DATA_HOME

Base data directory when R_USER_DATA_DIR is unset. On macOS, when both are unset, condathis uses ~/.local/share instead of the platform default under ~/Library/Application Support. The platform default contains a space, and micromamba run can fail on paths with spaces.

R_USER_CACHE_DIR, XDG_CACHE_HOME

Base cache directory, in that order. clean_cache() empties its R/condathis subdirectory.

HOME, USERPROFILE, APPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA

Home and application data directories. tools::R_user_dir() uses them when none of the variables above is set: on Windows, APPDATA for the data directory and LOCALAPPDATA for the cache directory.

condathis creates the condathis data directory only when a call needs it. Queries, such as list_envs(), env_exists(), list_packages() and validate_env(), create no environment and never install micromamba. get_install_dir() and get_env_dir() create only the data directory.

with_sandbox_dir() sets all the data and cache variables above to temporary directories. Environments, packages and the micromamba binary that condathis installs inside it, with every backend, then stay out of your own directories.

Environment variables for downloads

install_micromamba() downloads with curl::curl_download() when curl 5.0.0 or later is installed, and with utils::download.file() otherwise. Both honor the standard proxy variables, such as http_proxy, https_proxy, and no_proxy.

Environment variables set or cleared in child processes

Every process condathis starts, whether micromamba itself or a command run by run(), run_bin() or run_pipeline(), starts from a copy of the calling session's environment. condathis then applies the overrides below to that copy only. condathis never modifies the calling R session. A process that you start yourself does not get these overrides. Pass --no-rc and --no-env to micromamba or conda to ignore your own Conda settings.

Cleared or reset, so that the user's own Conda or Mamba setup does not interfere:

CONDARC, MAMBARC

Set to "". With the micromamba backend, condathis also calls micromamba with --no-env and with --rc-file pointing at condathis-micromamba.yaml in the condathis data directory. So micromamba ignores the user's configuration files and MAMBA_* settings. That file pins pkgs_dirs to the condathis package cache, and sets shortcuts: false, so that micromamba adds no Start Menu shortcuts on Windows. One exception: micromamba extracts packages in subprocesses (micromamba package extract) that it starts without these options. These subprocesses still read the user's configuration files, such as ~/.condarc, ~/.mambarc and those in XDG_CONFIG_HOME. They also read the MAMBA_* variables that are not listed here.

CONDA_ROOT_PREFIX, MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX

Set to "" for every command of an environment. MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX is set to "" also when the activation of the micromamba backend sets it, as it does on Windows. micromamba itself gets the condathis data directory as its root prefix, with -r and in MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX. Without MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX, micromamba (2.8.1 to 2.10.0 checked) refuses to start, even for --version, when its default root prefix exists but is not a Conda environment. The default root prefix is $XDG_DATA_HOME/mamba, else ~/.local/share/mamba, on Windows else mamba in the roaming application data folder.

CONDA_PREFIX, MAMBA_PREFIX, CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV, MAMBA_DEFAULT_ENV, CONDA_PROMPT_MODIFIER, MAMBA_PROMPT_MODIFIER

Set to "".

CONDA_SHLVL, MAMBA_SHLVL

Set to "0".

CONDA_PKGS_DIRS, MAMBA_PKGS_DIRS

For micromamba and the commands of its environments, environments given by env_path() included: the pkgs/ directory of the condathis data directory. Packages are cached only there. The user's own ~/.mamba/pkgs cache is never read or written, and clean_cache() never cleans it. For the commands of other backends' environments: the directory conda-pkgs/ next to the envs/ directory that holds the environment, in the backend's data directory. A Conda tool run in such an environment caches its packages there, and clean_cache() empties it. It is "" when the environment is not in a directory named envs. An environment given by env_path() that such a backend runs gets the backend's own conda-pkgs/, not one next to the environment. With activate = TRUE, the activation of such a backend can set another value (see register_backend()).

MAMBA_ENVS_PATH, MAMBA_ENVS_DIRS

Set to "".

CONDA_ENVS_DIRS

Removed from the child environment.

CONDA_ENVS_PATH

For micromamba and the commands of its environments, environments given by env_path() included: the envs/ directory of the condathis data directory. For the commands of other backends' environments: the parent directory of the environment, and for an environment given by env_path(), the backend's own envs/ directory. The value is the same with activate = TRUE and activate = FALSE. With activation, the backend can set another value.

R_HOME

Set to "", so an R installed in a Conda environment does not pick up the R installation of the calling session.

TMPDIR

Set to a new temporary directory for each call. condathis removes it when the call returns.

TMP

On Windows, for every micromamba command: a directory in its TMPDIR. micromamba writes its temporary files there, such as the batch files of micromamba run, so they are removed with that directory, also when the command is stopped. The activate.d scripts see this value while the activation is recorded. A value that they build from it names the session's TMP, unless they wrote something in that directory: then the value names that directory, which the command finds in its TMPDIR, and the activation is recorded again for every command. The commands of run(), run_bin() and run_pipeline() keep the session's value, unless an activate.d script sets one. TEMP is never changed.

XDG_CACHE_HOME

For every micromamba command: the cache/ directory of the condathis data directory. There micromamba keeps its repodata cache, instead of in ~/.cache/conda, and the mamba/proc directory of micromamba run. The scripts that packages run when they are installed or removed see this value too. The activate.d scripts, while the activation is recorded, and the commands of run(), run_bin() and run_pipeline() keep the session's value.

HOME (USERPROFILE on Windows)

For micromamba env list, micromamba env remove and, unless it needs your home directory, micromamba create: the home/ directory of the condathis data directory. So micromamba does not change ~/.conda/environments.txt (see Details in get_install_dir()). The scripts that packages run when they are installed or removed by these commands see this value too. On Windows, micromamba looks there for the Start Menu shortcuts of the removed packages.

PYTHONNOUSERSITE, PYTHONPATH, PYTHONHOME

For micromamba list, which list_packages() runs: PYTHONNOUSERSITE is "1" and the other two are removed, so pip reports only the packages of the environment.

With the default activate = TRUE of run(), run_bin() and run_pipeline(), condathis applies activation variables on top. For the micromamba backend, these are the variables that a real micromamba run activation sets. They include the variables from activate.d scripts shipped by the installed packages. These scripts run with the command's TMPDIR, user cache and working directory. condathis records the variables once per environment and R session. It reuses them until the environment (its packages, its activate.d scripts or env_vars.d files) or the session's environment variables change. It starts the command itself. Values that name the command's TMPDIR are recorded again for every command. Values that name the working directory are recorded again in another working directory. For other backends, the backend package sets the activation variables (see register_backend()).

With activate = FALSE, run_bin() applies no activation variables and only prepends the environment's binary directories to PATH. run_pipeline() sets this fixed set instead:

CONDA_PREFIX, CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV

The environment directory and its name. For an environment given by env_path(), the name is its directory.

CONDA_SHLVL, MAMBA_SHLVL

Set to "1".

CONDA_PROMPT_MODIFIER, MAMBA_PROMPT_MODIFIER

Set to "(<env_name>) ".

PATH

The environment's binary directories, prepended to the session PATH.

CONDA_ENVS_PATH is the same as with activate = TRUE: it comes from the clean variables above.

On Windows, variable names are matched case-insensitively. An override replaces any inherited spelling of the same name, such as Path.

micromamba discovery

condathis uses the first candidate that exists and reports a compatible version:

  1. The condathis.micromamba_path option.

  2. The CONDATHIS_MICROMAMBA_PATH environment variable.

  3. The binary managed by condathis, see micromamba_bin_path().

  4. A micromamba next to the running R, when R is installed in a Conda environment.

  5. A micromamba inside CONDA_PREFIX.

  6. A micromamba in the micromamba-env environment of the micromamba backend, <condathis data directory>/envs/micromamba-env. condathis ignores an environment of that name that another backend created.

  7. A micromamba on PATH.

When no candidate is compatible, install_micromamba() downloads the pinned version into the managed location.

Interactive sessions

condathis shows spinners for every verbose level except "silent", and only when rlang::is_interactive() returns TRUE. The same holds for the download progress of install_micromamba(). Set the rlang_interactive option to FALSE to turn them off in an interactive session.

See also

get_install_dir(), micromamba_bin_path(), install_micromamba(), with_sandbox_dir(), tools::R_user_dir(), condathis-conditions

Examples

# Set options in an .Rprofile file. For example, use a specific
# micromamba binary, and create new environments with the "rattler"
# backend when the rattlerthis package is installed (micromamba stays
# the fallback):
#   options(
#     condathis.micromamba_path = "/opt/micromamba/bin/micromamba",
#     condathis.backend_priority = c("rattler", "micromamba")
#   )
# The same binary, as a line of an .Renviron file:
#   CONDATHIS_MICROMAMBA_PATH=/opt/micromamba/bin/micromamba

# Redirect all condathis data to temporary directories
condathis::with_sandbox_dir({
  print(condathis::get_install_dir()$path)
})
#> [1] "/tmp/RtmpdmGzuA/condathis-sandbox-1a10423e3b19/data/R/condathis"
